measurements.note: The five buildings the arrêté names as the square's northern edge. It is the register's own enumeration and it is why this record is a `group`: what the node calls 'twin palaces' is, in the listing, a square bounded by five separately protected buildings.

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. `record_kind: group`, AND THE REASON IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. The corpus's exemplar is 'Place de la Concorde, twin palaces' - Gabriel's two colonnaded fronts framing the Rue Royale. In the Base Mérimée that object does not exist as one thing: PA00088880 lists the SQUARE and its own text EXCLUDES the buildings, defining the place as bounded by the Ministère de la Marine and the Hôtels Coislin, du Plessis-Bellière, Cartier and Crillon; each of those is separately listed under its own PA number and its own date (Crillon 1900, Coislin 1923). Three references are therefore carried and the record is declared a group. Only PA00088880 was extracted; the two hôtel notices are locators read from a Wikipedia list table and are not quoted. No rights line was read, so no `rights_evidence`.
